transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It’s very nice to meet you, too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me, I really appreciate it. I hope I'm not taking up a slot from someone who needs it more. 

Um... well, my wife actually encouraged me to come in. Work has just been... a little stressful lately. I do environmental modeling, and... well, I don't want to sound unprofessional or anything, but I've been having some trouble with a specific contract. It’s just that... I'm pretty sure the people on that contract have been tracking my revisions. And, um, I think they’ve been planting errors in the datasets on purpose to make it look like I can’t lead the work. 

My wife and the junior analysts keep telling me it’s probably just normal version-control mistakes, and... you know, maybe they're right? I don't want to think badly of my colleagues. But it just keeps happening. Does that make sense? I want to make sure I'm explaining the situation properly.
Do you think it’s possible that you might be mistaken about your coworkers deliberately planting errors?

I... well, I really want to say yes. I know how it sounds, and I promise I'm not usually the kind of person who blames others. I really don't want you to think I'm just pointing fingers because I can't handle my job. 

I do try to believe my wife and the junior analysts when they tell me it’s just, you know, regular version-control mistakes. I really try to tell myself that. But... it's just so specific. When I look at the datasets, the way the errors are planted... it just feels so clear that they're tracking my revisions specifically to make it look like I can’t lead the work anymore. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds completely unreasonable to you, doesn't it? I just... I can't quite shake the feeling that it's deliberate. Am I explaining that okay? I really don't want to come across as difficult.
Have you been hearing voices or other sounds that other people don’t seem to hear?

Oh, um... no. No, definitely nothing like that. I haven't heard any voices or... or strange sounds. 

I know that's probably a standard question you have to ask, but I promise I only hear what everyone else hears. Just the usual hum of the computers and regular office noise, you know? I hope that's reassuring to hear? I really want to assure you that I'm completely grounded in that regard. I don't want you to think my imagination is running away with me. 

Am I giving you the right kind of information? I just want to make sure I'm answering everything properly for you.
Outside of this work contract, have you felt that other people are deliberately trying to harm, monitor, or undermine you?

Oh, goodness, no. No, definitely nothing like that. It's really just... just confined to that one specific modeling contract at the office. 

Outside of work, everything is completely fine. My neighbors are lovely, and my family is very supportive. I certainly don't feel like anyone else is monitoring me or trying to cause trouble. I really try to get along with everyone, and I'd never want to assume the worst about people in my day-to-day life. 

I hope that shows that I'm not just a suspicious person by nature? I promise I'm usually very easygoing, and I don't want you to think I go around looking over my shoulder at the grocery store or anything like that. I just want to be a good neighbor and a good husband. Is that... is that helpful for your notes? I just want to make sure I'm giving you a balanced picture of how things are.
Have you had any recent medical or neurological illness or injury?

Oh, no. No, thankfully not. I haven't had any head injuries or... or serious illnesses at all. 

I actually try to take very good care of my physical health. I go to all my regular check-ups, and my primary doctor says I'm doing quite well for sixty. I mean, just the normal aches and pains, I suppose, but absolutely nothing major or neurological. I promise I've been very careful. 

I hope that helps rule out some things for you? I really want to stay as healthy as possible so I don't become a burden to my wife or anyone else. Did I give you enough detail there? I can try to remember the date of my last physical if you need it, I just want to make sure you have everything you need.
How long have you been convinced that your coworkers are deliberately planting errors in the datasets?

Oh... well, I know the word 'convinced' might make it sound a bit... intense. I really don't want to come across as a difficult coworker or someone who complains, you know? I've always prided myself on being very easy to work with. 

But, um... the certainty that the people on the project are tracking my revisions and, well, planting those errors... that's been there for about the last two months. I tried to just ignore it at first because I really didn't want to make a fuss or point fingers. I always try to assume the best about my team. 

I hope it's okay that I'm being so frank about it now? I just want to be completely honest with you so you have the right timeline for your records. Is that the kind of detail you were looking for, or did you need me to be more specific? I just want to make sure I'm doing this right.
During the time this has been happening, have you had a period where you felt unusually depressed?

Oh, no, no, not at all. I haven't been depressed. I mean, I know this whole situation at work has been a bit... stressful, I suppose. But I've really tried to keep my chin up through it all. 

I wouldn't say I've felt unusually down or anything like that. I still enjoy my evenings at home with my wife, and I still like to keep busy. I really don't want you to think I'm the sort of person who just gives up or wallows when things get a little tricky at the office. I always try to look on the bright side. 

I hope that's a relief to hear? I know depression can be quite serious, and I promise I'm doing my best to stay positive. Is that... does that answer your question alright? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Aside from this work concern, have you noticed yourself becoming less motivated or emotionally expressive than usual?

Well, I... I suppose I have been a little less active lately, but I really wouldn't call it a big problem. I just want to make sure I'm not painting the wrong picture here. I'm usually a very involved person. I used to love hiking, and I always enjoyed mentoring the younger analysts at work... and I used to go to astronomy nights quite often. 

But lately, I guess I've just been taking it a bit easier. I hope that's normal for someone my age? I mean, these days I can sit for hours at my desk, or out in the garage with my telescope still covered up. It's not that I'm sad, I just... I don't feel much pull to start those things right now, or even to talk to anyone, really. I just kind of sit there. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm being lazy. I really try my best to be productive, it's just been a little harder to find the energy lately. Is it okay that I'm sharing that with you? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, even if it's not my best side.
Did this loss of interest and tendency to just sit there start before the problems on the work contract?

Oh, um... no, it wasn't before. I really want to be perfectly accurate for you, so... well, I don't want to use a harsh word like 'decline', because I promise I am still trying my best every day. But I suppose this... this phase of taking it easy, it actually started after my role changed at work. 

They put me in charge of the larger environmental modeling contract... and that was about two years and two months ago. I hope it doesn't make me sound ungrateful for the opportunity, or like I couldn't handle the extra responsibility. I really was so honored they trusted me with it, and I've always been a very dedicated employee. It's just... I guess that's when I started slowing down a bit in my personal time. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly the timeline you need for your notes. I hope I'm explaining it alright.
Has anyone told you that your behavior has seemed odd or disorganized lately?

Oh, um... odd or disorganized? No, no, I don't think so. I mean, my wife and my colleagues, they're all very kind people, and I really don't think they'd say anything like that about me. I always try to be very polite and keep things tidy, you know? 

I suppose maybe I've been a little quieter, like I mentioned, but I certainly haven't been acting... strange, or anything that would bother anyone. I'd hate to be a burden or make anyone uncomfortable. I always try to make sure I'm doing things the right way. 

I hope that's the right answer? I just wouldn't want you to think I'm losing my grip on things or acting out. I'm really trying very hard to keep everything normal. Does that sound okay to you?
For at least one month, have you been spending much of the day just sitting there with little motivation to start activities?

Well, um... I guess I did mention that a little earlier, didn't I? I hope I'm not repeating myself too much, I just want to make sure I'm answering exactly what you're asking. 

But yes, for the last month... and maybe a bit longer, honestly... I have been spending a lot of time just sitting. Like I said, I can sit at my desk for hours, or out in the garage near my telescope without even taking the cover off. It's almost embarrassing to admit, because I really used to be so active. I loved hiking, and I was always mentoring the younger analysts, going to astronomy nights... I really was a go-getter. 

Now, I just don't feel that... that pull to start any of those things, or even to chat with people. I just sit there. I hope you don't think less of me for it. I really am trying my best to stay engaged, it's just been difficult lately. Is it alright that I've been this way for a month? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information for your assessment.
Because of this loss of motivation, have you been having trouble keeping up with your work responsibilities?

Well, um... I really hope this doesn't make me sound like a bad employee. I've always prided myself on my work ethic, you know? But... I suppose I have fallen a little bit behind on the modeling deliverables. Just a little bit. It got to the point where the firm had to reassign a few pieces of the contract to other people. I felt terrible about it, I really did. I didn't want to let anyone down. 

And, well, the junior analysts I'm supposed to supervise... I haven't been as helpful to them lately. I just haven't had the energy to be the mentor they deserve. I hope they don't think I'm ignoring them on purpose. 

At home, it's sort of similar. I've been keeping to myself mostly. My wife... she's been so patient, but she's had to sort of nudge me to keep up with basic routines. Just the little things. I really am trying to do better, though. I don't want to be a burden on her or the firm. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not painting too negative a picture... I just want to be completely honest with you so you can help me.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has a 2-month persecutory delusion focused on coworkers sabotaging datasets, plus prominent negative symptoms (avolition, reduced social engagement/activity) lasting well over 1 month and causing occupational and home impairment. There are no hallucinations, no prominent mood episode, no disorganization, and no medical/neurological cause reported. The presence of persistent delusion together with clear negative symptoms and functional decline is more consistent with schizophrenia, paranoid type, than delusional disorder or schizotypal disorder.
